questions.question: Does the reconciliation readout compute a real content-token count via a genuine tokenize()/steps[0..i)-filtering pipeline, rather than a placeholder/stand-in constant, a hardcoded 'difference equals template overhead' label with no real subtraction, or a load-bearing dependency on S3's backend-client.tokenize() that silently degrades to a fixed or zero count when tokenize() is unavailable (e.g. the WebSocket is offline) without surfacing that degradation to the user as an explicit unavailable state?

Per Implementation Constraint 5, the reconciliation's step-filtering logic must mirror toOllamaMessages' rules independently, since chat-workspace.tsx (src/) cannot import server/ollama-client.ts's toOllamaMessages across the tsconfig-enforced server/src boundary. Confirm the reconciliation filtering is implemented as its own function (ideally in a lib helper, per the story's notes, to preserve chat-workspace.tsx's line budget) whose logic matches toOllamaMessages' filtering rules (server/ollama-client.ts ~245-301 — e.g. its tool_call/tool_result/system-step handling) rather than importing across the boundary or silently diverging from those rules.

Could `workspace` be deleted and rewritten without modifying any file outside its `dependencies_allowed` list? If not, which cross-module dependencies exist and do they flow through declared seam contracts in architecture.md?

Do tests cover, as distinct assertions: (a) AC-UX-5's │-separated request-preview rendering reusing S2's TokenSeparatorFormatter export from src/lib/token-view.ts (not a separator formatter re-implemented locally in this story), (b) the verbatim chat-template string display sourced from POST /api/show's `template` field, distinct from the pre-existing model-metadata dialog's own template display (chat-workspace.tsx ~3039), (c) AC-UX-6's three-figure reconciliation display asserting the actual overhead-label text (not just that three numbers render), and (d) the tool_call-turn unavailable-with-named-reason path?

Per the adversarial review's specific trap: reconciliation must filter via toOllamaMessages' rules, never the displayed OpenAI-shaped requestJsonPreview (which uses buildOpenAIRequestBody/toOpenAIMessages, chat-workspace.tsx ~918-935). Show a test that would fail if the reconciliation implementation were swapped to simply count tokens in requestJsonPreview's rendered string instead — e.g. a fixture conversation containing a system step and a tool_call/tool_result pair, where toOllamaMessages' filtering and toOpenAIMessages' filtering produce a different effective message set, and the reconciliation count must match the toOllamaMessages-filtered figure, not the OpenAI-shaped one. Evidence: currently `grep -in "reconcil" src/components/chat-workspace.tsx` matches nothing; post-implementation the reconciliation function/identifier must exist and must not reference `requestJsonPreview` or `buildOpenAIRequestBody` in its own computation path.

The request-preview panel now displays the model's chat-template string verbatim, sourced from an external server (POST /api/show) that a misconfigured OLLAMA_URL could point at an untrusted host. Confirm this string is rendered as literal text — never interpreted as HTML/markdown, no dangerouslySetInnerHTML — consistent with how modelMeta.template is already displayed elsewhere in this component via the existing renderTextSection pattern (chat-workspace.tsx ~3039), so this new display site introduces no HTML-injection surface.

AC-UX-5 requires the request-preview panel to render outgoing message contents with │ separators and to display /api/show's `template` field verbatim, never a reconstructed template. Show: (a) the panel's new separator-rendering code reusing S2's exported formatTokens/token-view.ts utility (currently `grep -n "token-view" src/components/chat-workspace.tsx` matches nothing; post-implementation it must show an import near the request-preview section), (b) the verbatim template field display distinct from any app-side template reconstruction, and (c) confirmation the test is not a pure mock-spy proxy that only checks a prop was passed without checking the rendered DOM text.

AC-UX-6 requires displaying the computed content-token count, the reported prompt_eval_count, and their difference labelled as chat-template overhead — never as a mismatch/error/warning — with tool_call-containing turns reporting reconciliation-unavailable with a named reason. Show: (a) the three-figure display code and the exact label text used for the difference, (b) a test asserting the label text does not contain 'mismatch', 'error', or 'warning', and (c) the tool_call-turn detection code and its distinct unavailable-with-reason rendering, grounded in Implementation Constraint 4 (compactSteps drops the empty assistant step; ws-handler.ts:163-171 mints a synthetic no-usage replacement, so only the final loop iteration reliably carries usage).

AC-TOK-5 (live-gated) requires, for a system+user-only conversation, the computed content-token count to be strictly less than Ollama's reported prompt_eval_count for the chat request built from those steps, with the difference equal to the template scaffolding's token count, computed from steps[0..i) — the steps preceding the assistant step carrying usage — filtered exactly as toOllamaMessages filters them, never from the live requestJsonPreview (which includes the assistant step itself and uses toOpenAIMessages filtering). Show the live-gated test, its gating against the same AC-ERR-3 mechanism, and confirm the computed figure comes from the reconciliation function verified in VQ-S4-002/VQ-S4-005 rather than any reference to requestJsonPreview.

AC-STRUCT-3 (cross-cutting, spanned by S2, S3, S4) caps the net line count added to src/components/chat-workspace.tsx by this entire epic — S2's toggle/switch/render-branch, S3's minimal wiring (if any), and S4's request-preview panel additions — at 60, measured as `git diff --numstat 4568f350ee65a73824efc56b2f9a524eacde71f2 -- src/components/chat-workspace.tsx | awk '{print $1-$2}'` (insertions minus deletions, not --stat's combined figure), against the baseline_sha recorded in epic-state.json (currently this command against the unmodified tree produces no output line, since HEAD equals the baseline SHA). Run this exact command after S4 lands — the last story in story_order to touch this file — and confirm the resulting net-line figure is at most 60. Also confirm the separator formatting, boundary-source resolution, whitespace-marker logic, and debounced tokenize round trip all live in src/lib/token-view.ts and its useTokenBoundaries hook, not inline in chat-workspace.tsx (cross-reference VQ-S2-002).
